data.narrative:
Collaborative Robotics, founded by Brad Porter, is a Series B robotics and manufacturing company that has raised $150M+ to date. The valuation analysis draws on a peer set of three same-stage, same-sector private comparables (Generalist AI at $2.0B, Bedrock Robotics at $1.8B, and Dexterity at $1.6B) alongside one public comparable and a broader universe of eight private peers including Divergent and Exotec.

Two triangulation methods were applied. The stage-progression method, anchored to the company's last post-money valuation of $500M, applies a 1.9x step-up multiplier typical for Series B advancement, yielding $950M. The peer-median method references the three same-stage, same-sector comparables, which demonstrate a median valuation of $1.8B with a range of $1.6B to $2.0B. This reflects both the maturity profile of peer businesses at identical stage and sector positioning.

The two methods triangulate to a valuation range of $808M (low) to $2.0B (high), with a median of $1.4B. The wide spread reflects material variance between forward-looking peer multiples and recent-stage progression dynamics. Key uncertainties include the strength of Collaborative Robotics' unit economics relative to named peers, capital efficiency trajectory post-Series B, and near-term customer concentration. The peer-median result of $1.8B carries greater weight given direct comparability on stage and sector.
